summary: South America's largest country and economy, an agricultural and resource superpower, and a leading voice of the Global South. A founding BRICS member pursuing non-alignment and multipolarity while stewarding the Amazon rainforest.

history.detail: Pedro Álvares Cabral claims Brazil; three centuries of colonial rule and slavery follow.
Dom Pedro I declares independence from Portugal, founding an empire.
Brazil is the last country in the Americas to end slavery.
Military coup ends the monarchy; the 'Old Republic' begins.
US-backed generals seize power; 21 years of dictatorship and repression.
Civilian rule restored; new constitution follows in 1988.
New currency tames hyperinflation and stabilises the economy.
Social programmes lift tens of millions out of poverty during a commodity boom.
Political crisis amid the Car Wash corruption scandal.
Defeats Bolsonaro; days later, supporters storm government buildings in Brasília.

alliances: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States

finance.currency_role: Brazilian real; largest economy in Latin America
finance.central_bank: Banco Central do Brasil (1964); known for high interest rates

tech_startups.vc_ecosystem: Largest in Latin America; fintech-led boom

resources.oil_gas: Major producer; vast offshore pre-salt oil fields; Petrobras state champion
resources.agriculture: World's top exporter of soy, beef, coffee, sugar and orange juice
resources.rare_earths: Holds among the largest reserves globally; developing extraction
resources.water: ~12% of the world's fresh water; Amazon and Guarani aquifer

follow_the_money.detail: China is Brazil's top trading partner, buying huge volumes of soy, iron ore and oil.
Central-bank instant-payment system used by most adults, disrupting card networks.
Lula pushes for trade in local currencies to reduce dollar reliance.

theories_disputed.detail: Declassified files show Washington backed the military coup (Operation Brother Sam) against a leftist government.
Cattle ranching and agribusiness are documented drivers; the scale of illegal versus legal clearing is contested.

connections.detail: Largest trading partner; commodities for investment
Democratic partner but independent foreign policy
Migration crisis and Essequibo border tensions on its frontier
Fellow BRICS voice of the Global South
